title: Onlayn muloqot va ijtimoiy tarmoqlar
goal_uz: Dars oxirida ingliz tilida onlayn to‘g‘ri muloqot qila olasiz: chat qisqartmalarini va emoji madaniyatini, izoh va sharhlarni, LinkedIn kabi professional xabarlarni yozishni hamda internet odobini o‘rganasiz.

vocab.uz: imkon qadar tez (as soon as possible)

scenes.title: Bugun: onlayn muloqot

examples.t: Did you see my message? It went viral.

scenes.say_native: Assalomu alaykum! Oldingi darsda yangiliklar va podkastlarni tinglashni o‘rgangandik. Bugun ingliz tilida onlayn muloqot qilishni o‘rganamiz — chat qisqartmalari, emoji madaniyati, izoh va sharhlar, professional xabarlar va tarmoq odobi. Bu ko‘nikmalar sizga ish va ijtimoiy tarmoqlarda juda kerak. Boshlaymiz.
scenes.say: Welcome back! Last time we covered news and podcasts. Today it's online communication: chat abbreviations, emoji culture, comments and reviews, professional networking messages and online politeness. By the end, you'll write all of these confidently. Let's begin.
scenes.say_uz: Qaytganingiz bilan! O‘tgan darsda yangiliklar va podkastlarni ko‘rib chiqqandik. Bugun onlayn muloqot: chat qisqartmalari, emoji madaniyati, izoh va sharhlar, professional tarmoq xabarlari va onlayn odobi. Dars oxirida bularning hammasini bemalol yozasiz. Boshlaymiz.

scenes.title: Nega onlayn muloqot muhim?
board: Tone is easy to misread online
scenes.say_native: Bugungi kunda ishning katta qismi yozma shaklda bo‘ladi: chatlar, emaillar, sharhlar, LinkedIn. Muammo shundaki, yozma matnda ohangni osongina noto‘g‘ri o‘qib qo‘yasiz. O‘zbek tilida ham shunday: “Qisqacha ayt” deyish o‘rniga chatda “Qisqa” deb yozsangiz, odam g‘azablangani deb o‘ylashi mumkin. Ingliz tilida bu masala yanada muhimroq, chunki siz ona tilida bo‘lmagansiz — shuning uchun qoidalar aniq bo‘lishi kerak.
scenes.say: Work happens in writing now: chats, emails, reviews, LinkedIn. The danger is tone — written words are easy to misread. In Uzbek the same thing happens. In English it matters even more, because the reader can't hear you. That's why we learn the rules.
scenes.say_uz: Ish bugungi kunda yozma shaklda: chatlar, emaillar, sharhlar, LinkedIn. Xatar — ohang: yozilgan gaplarni noto‘g‘ri o‘qib qo‘yish oson. O‘zbek tilida ham shunday. Ingliz tilida esa bu yanada muhimroq, chunki o‘quvchi sizni eshitmaydi. Shuning uchun qoidalarni o‘rganamiz.

scenes.title: Chat qisqartmalari
board: LOL — laughing out loud — qattiq kulish
BRB — be right back — hozir qaytaman
ASAP — as soon as possible — imkon qadar tez
FYI — for your information — ma’lumot uchun

examples.t: Can you send the report ASAP?
examples.uz: Hisobotni imkon qadar tez yubora olasizmi?

scenes.say_native: Chat qisqartmalari ingliz tilida juda ko‘p. Eng kerakli beshtasi: LOL — “laughing out loud” — qattiq kulib yuborish. BRB — “be right back” — hozir qaytaman. ASAP — “as soon as possible” — imkon qadar tez. FYI — “for your information” — ma’lumot uchun. DM — “direct message” — shaxsiy xabar. Bularni professional va norasmiy chatda ham uchratasiz.
scenes.say: Five abbreviations you'll see everywhere: LOL — laughing out loud. BRB — be right back. ASAP — as soon as possible. FYI — for your information. DM — direct message, a private message. You'll meet these in both casual and work chats.
scenes.say_uz: Hammangiz ko‘rib turadigan beshta qisqartma: LOL — qattiq kulish. BRB — hozir qaytaman. ASAP — imkon qadar tez. FYI — ma’lumot uchun. DM — shaxsiy xabar. Bularni ham norasmiy, ham ish chatlarida uchratasiz.

scenes.title: Qisqartmalarni o‘qib tushuning
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Beshta qisqartmani inglizcha to‘liq shaklida ayting: LOL, BRB, ASAP, FYI, DM. Keyin ularning o‘zbekcha ma’nosini ayting. Baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: Say these aloud: LOL, BRB, ASAP, FYI, DM. Then say the full English form of each, then the Uzbek meaning.
scenes.say_uz: Bularni baland ovozda ayting: LOL, BRB, ASAP, FYI, DM. Keyin har birining inglizcha to‘liq shakli va o‘zbekcha ma’nosini ayting.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: LOL — laughing out loud — qattiq kulish
BRB — be right back — hozir qaytaman
ASAP — as soon as possible — imkon qadar tez
FYI — for your information — ma’lumot uchun
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: LOL — “laughing out loud” — qattiq kulish. BRB — “be right back” — hozir qaytaman. ASAP — “as soon as possible” — imkon qadar tez. FYI — “for your information” — ma’lumot uchun. DM — “direct message” — shaxsiy xabar. Endi ko‘proq qisqartma o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say: Answers: LOL — laughing out loud. BRB — be right back. ASAP — as soon as possible. FYI — for your information. DM — direct message. Now five more.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: LOL — “laughing out loud” — qattiq kulish. BRB — “be right back” — hozir qaytaman. ASAP — “as soon as possible” — imkon qadar tez. FYI — “for your information” — ma’lumot uchun. DM — “direct message” — shaxsiy xabar. Endi yana beshta.

scenes.title: Yana beshta qisqartma

examples.t: BTW, the meeting moved to Thursday.

scenes.say_native: Yana beshta qisqartma: IMHO — “in my humble opinion” — mening kamtarona fikrim. BTW — “by the way” — aytmoqchi. OOO — “out of office” — ofisda yo‘q (dam olishda). EOD — “end of day” — kun oxirigacha. TBD — “to be decided” — qaror qabul qilinmagan. Bu qisqartmalar email va chatda ko‘p uchraydi. Endi mashq qilamiz.
scenes.say: Five more: IMHO — in my humble opinion. BTW — by the way. OOO — out of office. EOD — end of day. TBD — to be decided, not yet decided. You'll see these in emails and work chats.
scenes.say_uz: Yana beshta: IMHO — mening kamtarona fikrim. BTW — aytmoqchi. OOO — ofisda yo‘q. EOD — kun oxirigacha. TBD — qaror qilinmagan. Bularni emaillarda va ish chatlarida ko‘rasiz.

scenes.title: Yana qisqartmalarni ayting
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Beshta qisqartmani baland ovozda inglizcha to‘liq shaklida ayting: IMHO, BTW, OOO, EOD, TBD. Keyin o‘zbek tilida ma’nosini ayting.
scenes.say: Say these aloud: IMHO, BTW, OOO, EOD, TBD. Say the full English form of each, then the Uzbek meaning.
scenes.say_uz: Bularni baland ovozda ayting: IMHO, BTW, OOO, EOD, TBD. Har birining to‘liq inglizcha shaklini, keyin o‘zbekcha ma’nosini ayting.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: IMHO — in my humble opinion — mening kamtarona fikrim
OOO — out of office — ofisda yo‘q
EOD — end of day — kun oxirigacha
TBD — to be decided — qaror qilinmagan
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: IMHO — mening kamtarona fikrim, BTW — aytmoqchi, OOO — ofisda yo‘q, EOD — kun oxirigacha, TBD — qaror qilinmagan. Qoida: qisqartmani ishlatishdan oldin o‘ylab ko‘ring — norasmiy chatda bemalol, rasmiy emailda ehtiyot bo‘ling.
scenes.say: Answers: IMHO — in my humble opinion; BTW — by the way; OOO — out of office; EOD — end of day; TBD — to be decided. Rule of thumb: abbreviations are fine in casual chat, but be careful in formal emails.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: IMHO — mening kamtarona fikrim; BTW — aytmoqchi; OOO — ofisda yo‘q; EOD — kun oxirigacha; TBD — qaror qilinmagan. Qoida: qisqartmalarni norasmiy chatda bemalol ishlating, rasmiy emailda ehtiyot bo‘ling.

scenes.title: Keng tarqalgan xato: HAMMASINI KATTA HARF BILAN YOZISH
board: ✓ Could you send the report as soon as you can?

examples.t: Writing in caps is like shouting at someone.
examples.uz: Katta harfda yozish birovga baqirayotgandek tuyuladi.

scenes.say_native: Keng tarqalgan xato: hamma harflarni katta yozish. Ingliz tilida katta harf bilan yozilgan matn baqirayotgan odamdek o‘qiladi. Jamoangiz chidashi mumkin, lekin mijoz bunday emas. Shuning uchun “I NEED THE REPORT NOW!!!” emas — “Could you send the report as soon as you can, please?” deb yozing. Endi shu xatoni to‘g‘rilang mashqida.
scenes.say: Writing in all caps reads like shouting. Your team might tolerate it, but a client won't. Instead of “I NEED THE REPORT NOW!!!” write “Could you send the report as soon as you can, please?” — same urgency, no aggression.
scenes.say_uz: Hamma harflarni katta yozish baqirayotganga o‘xshaydi. Jamoa chidashi mumkin, lekin mijoz emas. “I NEED THE REPORT NOW!!!” o‘rniga “Could you send the report as soon as you can, please?” deb yozing — xuddi shu shoshilinchlik, lekin bosiq ohang.

scenes.title: Gapni yumshoq qilib yozing
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Ikki tajovuzkor gapni yumshoqroq qilib yozing: “SEND THE FILE NOW.” “WHERE ARE YOU?” Ingliz tilida so‘rang, baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: Soften these two messages: “SEND THE FILE NOW.” “WHERE ARE YOU?” Turn them into polite requests and say them aloud.
scenes.say_uz: Ikki tajovuzkor gapni yumshoqqa aylantiring: “SEND THE FILE NOW.” “WHERE ARE YOU?” Ularni muloyim iltimos qilib yozib, baland ovozda ayting.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: Could you send the file when you get a chance, please?
Just checking in — where are you? No rush.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: “Could you send the file when you get a chance, please?” — “Fayl yubora olasizmi?” — muloyim. Ikkinchisi: “Just checking in — where are you? No rush.” — “Vaziyatni bilmoqchi edim — qayerdasiz? Shoshilish yo‘q.” O‘zbek tilida ham shunday yumshoqlik kerak. Endi emoji madaniyatiga o‘tamiz.
scenes.say: Answers: “Could you send the file when you get a chance, please?” And “Just checking in — where are you? No rush.” The same softness works in Uzbek too. Now emoji culture.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: “Could you send the file when you get a chance, please?” Va “Just checking in — where are you? No rush.” xuddi shunday yumshoqlik o‘zbek tilida ham ishlaydi. Endi emoji madaniyati.

scenes.title: Emoji madaniyati
board: 🙂 = polite, not sarcastic, in UK English
scenes.say_native: Emoji madaniyati: ingliz tilida, ayniqsa Britaniya ish muhitida, 🙂 — tabassum, bu g‘amho‘rlik va muloyimlikni bildiradi — kinoya emas. 👍 — “tushundim, kelishdik” degani. 😂 — chindan kulgili narsa, haddan tashqari ishlatmang. Ishda 🙃, 😜, 🤪 kabi chalkash emojilarni ishlatmang. Va e’tibor bering: emoji norasmiy — mijozga birinchi xatda emoji ishlatmang.
scenes.say: Emoji culture in UK English: the slightly smiling face is polite, not sarcastic. The thumbs up means “agreed, received.” The laughing face means genuinely funny — use it sparingly. Avoid confusing emojis at work, and don't open a first message to a client with an emoji.
scenes.say_uz: Britaniya ingliz tilida emoji madaniyati: ozgina tabassum — muloyimlik, kinoya emas. Bosh barmog‘i — “tushundim, kelishdik”. Kula yuz — chindan kulgili — kam ishlating. Ishda chalkash emojilardan — 🙃, 😜 — saqlaning. Mijozga birinchi xatda emoji ishlatmang.

scenes.title: Qaysi emoji o‘rinli?
board: 2. A colleague sends a genuinely funny meme. → ?
3. A client's first email to you. → ?
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Uchta holat uchun to‘g‘ri emoji tanlang: menejeringiz yig‘ilishni tasdiqladi; hamkasbingiz chindan kulgili mem yubordi; mijozdan birinchi xat keldi. Baland ovozda javob bering: qaysi emoji?
scenes.say: Choose the right emoji for three situations: your manager confirms the meeting; a colleague sends a genuinely funny picture; a client emails you for the first time. Say your answers aloud.
scenes.say_uz: Uchta holat uchun to‘g‘ri emojini tanlang: menejeringiz yig‘ilishni tasdiqladi; hamkasbingiz chindan kulgili surat yubordi; mijoz birinchi marta yozdi. Javoblaringizni baland ovozda ayting.

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: menejer tasdiqlaganda — 👍 yoki emoji yo‘q. Kulgili suratga — 😂. Mijozga birinchi xatda — emoji ishlatmang, matnni muloyim yozing. Endi chat suhbatini o‘qiymiz.
scenes.say: Answers: manager confirms — thumbs up or no emoji. Funny picture — laughing face. First client email — no emoji, keep it formal. Now a real chat.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: menejer tasdiqladi — 👍 yoki emoji yo‘q. Kulgili surat — 😂. Birinchi xat — emoji yo‘q, rasmiy ohang. Endi haqiqiy chatni o‘qiymiz.

scenes.title: Haqiqiy chat: loyiha uchrashuvi
board: Priya: Hi, are we still on for Thursday's review?
Priya: 3 pm works. I'll bring the draft.
scenes.say_native: O‘qing. Priya bilan bo‘lgan ish chatini baland ovozda ingliz tilida o‘qib chiqing. E’tibor bering: qisqa gaplar, savol-javob tartibi, oxirida 🙂 muloyimlik belgisi.
scenes.say: Priya: Hi, are we still on for Thursday's review? You: Yes — 3 pm, right? Priya: 3 pm works. I'll bring the draft. You: Perfect. See you then.
scenes.say_uz: Priya: Salom, payshanba ko‘rib chiqish uchrashuvi qoladimi? Siz: Ha — soat 3mi? Priya: Soat 3 bo‘ladi. Qoralama olib kelaman. Siz: Ajoyib. Ko‘rishguncha.

scenes.title: Chatga javob yozing
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Priya “I'll bring the draft” — “Qoralama olib kelaman” degan xabarga ikki xil javob yozing: norasmiy va ishbop. Baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: Priya says “I'll bring the draft.” Write two replies: one casual and one professional. Say them aloud.
scenes.say_uz: Priya “I'll bring the draft” — “Qoralama olib kelaman” deb yozdi. Ikki xil javob yozing: biri norasmiy, biri ishbop. Baland ovozda ayting.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: Professional: Thanks, Priya — Thursday at 3 works for me.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: norasmiy — “Sounds good 🙂” yoki “Great, thanks!”; ishbop — “Thanks, Priya — Thursday at 3 works for me.” — “Rahmat, Priya — payshanba soat 3 menga to‘g‘ri keladi.” Ikkalasi ham to‘g‘ri, farq — ohangda. Endi izoh va sharhlarga o‘tamiz.
scenes.say: Answers: casual — “Sounds good” with a smiley; professional — “Thanks, Priya — Thursday at 3 works for me.” Both are correct; only the tone differs. Now comments and reviews.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: norasmiy — “Sounds good” tabassumli yuz bilan; ishbop — “Thanks, Priya — Thursday at 3 works for me.” Ikkalasi ham to‘g‘ri — farq faqat ohangda. Endi izoh va sharhlar.

scenes.title: Izohlar va sharhlar: nima qilish va nimadan tiyilish
board: Say what + why + what you'd recommend
Avoid: rants, personal attacks, ALL CAPS

examples.t: Great location, but the room was small.
examples.uz: Joyi zo‘r, lekin xona kichik edi.

scenes.say_native: Sharh yozishning tuzilishi bor: nima qilganingizni, nega yaxshi yoki yomon bo‘lganini va boshqalarga nima maslahat berishingizni ayting. Aniq misollar yozing: “xodimlar mehribon”, “Wi-Fi tez”, “xona juda kichik”. Quyidagilardan tiyilish: norozi chorlovlari, shaxsiy hujumlar, katta harflarda yozish. O‘zbek tilida ham sharhlar xuddi shunday tuziladi.
scenes.say: A good review has a structure: what you experienced, why it was good or bad, and what you'd recommend to others. Be specific — “fast Wi-Fi, friendly staff.” Avoid rants, personal attacks and ALL CAPS. Uzbek reviews work the same way.
scenes.say_uz: Yaxshi sharhning tuzilishi bor: nima qilganingiz, nega yaxshi yoki yomon bo‘lgani va boshqalarga nima maslahat berishingiz. Aniq misollar yozing — “xodimlar mehribon”, “Wi-Fi tez”. Norozi chorlovlardan, shaxsiy hujumlardan va katta harflardan tiyiling. O‘zbek tilida ham shunday.

scenes.title: Sharh namunasi: mehmonxona
board: Stayed two nights for work. Clean rooms, fast Wi-Fi and a five-minute walk to the station. Breakfast was basic, but the staff couldn't have been kinder. Would stay again.
scenes.say_native: Tinglang. Mehmonxona uchun yozilgan to‘rtta yulduzli sharhni ovoz chiqarib o‘qing. E’tibor bering: qancha tun qolgani, nima yoqqan, nima yoqmagan, qaytarmisiz.
scenes.say: Stayed two nights for work. Clean rooms, fast Wi-Fi and a five-minute walk to the station. Breakfast was basic, but the staff couldn't have been kinder. Would stay again.
scenes.say_uz: Ish uchun ikki kecha qoldim. Xonalar toza, Wi-Fi tez va vokzalgacha besh daqiqalik piyoda. Nonushta oddiy edi, lekin xodimlar juda mehribon. Yana qolaman.

scenes.title: Restoran uchun uch yulduzli sharh yozing
board: You visited once. Food was good, service was slow.
scenes.say_native: Mashq. O‘zingiz restoranga borganingizni tasavvur qiling: taomlar yaxshi edi, xizmat sekin. Uch yulduzli sharh yozing — uch-to‘rt gap. Baland ovozda o‘qing.
scenes.say: Imagine you visited a restaurant: the food was good but the service was slow. Write a three-star review, three or four sentences. Read it aloud.
scenes.say_uz: Tasavvur qiling: restoranga bordingiz — taomlar yaxshi edi, xizmat sekin. Uch yulduzli sharh yozing, uch-to‘rt jumlada. Baland ovozda o‘qing.

scenes.title: Namunaviy javob
board: The food was excellent, but we waited forty minutes for the mains. The staff apologised, but it took too long. Come here for the food, not the speed.
scenes.say_native: Namunaviy javob: “Good food, slow service — 3 stars. The food was excellent, but we waited forty minutes for the mains. The staff apologised, but it took too long. Come here for the food, not the speed.” — “Taom zo‘r, xizmat sekin — 3 yulduz. Taom ajoyib edi, lekin asosiy taomlar uchun qirq daqiqa kutdik. Xodimlar uzr so‘rashdi, lekin bu juda uzoq bo‘ldi. Bu yerga taom uchun keling, tezlik uchun emas.” Qisqa, aniq, adolatli. Endi salbiy sharhlarga javob berishni o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say: A strong answer: “Good food, slow service — 3 stars. The food was excellent, but we waited forty minutes for the mains. The staff apologised, but it took too long. Come here for the food, not the speed.” Short, specific, fair. Now — responding to negative reviews.
scenes.say_uz: Yaxshi javob: “Good food, slow service — 3 stars. The food was excellent, but we waited forty minutes for the mains. The staff apologised, but it took too long. Come here for the food, not the speed.” Qisqa, aniq, adolatli. Endi — salbiy sharhlarga javob berish.

scenes.title: Salbiy sharhga biznes javobi

examples.t: We're sorry to hear this — please DM us and we'll make it right.
examples.uz: Bundan afsusdamiz — bizga shaxsiy xabar yozing, tuzaltamiz.

scenes.say_native: Biznes sifatida salbiy sharhga javob berish san’ati bor: avval e’tirof eting — “We're sorry to hear this” — e’tirozni emas, taassurotni qabul qiling. E’tirof etib, uzr so‘rang, keyin tuzatish taklif qiling. Va eng muhimi: masalani shaxsiy xabarga o‘tkazing — hamma oldida bahslashmang. O‘zbek tilida ham shunday: “Notapashtiz, shaxsiy xabar yozing, tuzatamiz.”
scenes.say: Responding as a business to a bad review has an art to it: first acknowledge — “We're sorry to hear this.” Acknowledge the experience, don't argue. Then apologise, then offer to fix it. Most importantly, take it offline — don't argue in public. The Uzbek version works the same way.
scenes.say_uz: Biznes sifatida salbiy sharhga javob berish san’ati bor: avval e’tirof eting — “We're sorry to hear this.” Taassurotni qabul qiling, bahslashmang. Keyin uzr so‘rang, keyin tuzatish taklif qiling. Eng muhimi — shaxsiy xabarga o‘tkazing, hamma oldida bahslashmang. O‘zbek tilida ham shunday.

scenes.title: Salbiy sharhga javob yozing
board: Your reply as the restaurant owner: ?
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Salbiy sharhga restoran egasi sifatida javob yozing: “Terrible meal, rude waiter.” — “Taom yomon, ofitsiant qo‘pol.” E’tirof eting, uzr so‘rang, shaxsiy xabarga o‘tkazing. Baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: Write a reply as the restaurant owner to this review: “Terrible meal, rude waiter.” Acknowledge it, apologise, and take it offline. Say it aloud.
scenes.say_uz: Quyidagi sharhga restoran egasi sifatida javob yozing: “Terrible meal, rude waiter.” — “Taom yomon, ofitsiant qo‘pol.” E’tirof eting, uzr so‘rang, shaxsiy xabarga o‘tkazing. Baland ovozda ayting.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: We're sorry to hear this. This isn't our standard.
Please DM us — we'd like to make it right.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: “We're sorry to hear this. This isn't the experience we aim for. Please DM us — we'd like to make it right.” — “Bundan afsusdamiz. Bu bizning standartimiz emas. Bizga shaxsiy xabar yozing — tuzaltamiz.” Va imzolang: egasi nomi bilan. Endi LinkedIn va professional tarmoqlarga o‘tamiz.
scenes.say: Answers: “We're sorry to hear this. This isn't the experience we aim for. Please DM us — we'd like to make it right.” And sign it with your name. Now professional networking.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: “We're sorry to hear this. This isn't the experience we aim for. Please DM us — we'd like to make it right.” Va imzolang, o‘z nomingiz bilan. Endi LinkedIn va professional tarmoqlar.

scenes.title: Keng tarqalgan xato: xato ohangda yozish
board: ✓ Hello Mr Karimov, I'm writing to apply for the analyst role.
No slang, no caps, no “u” for “you”
scenes.say_native: Keng tarqalgan xato: professional xatda norasmiy uslub. “HELLO SIR, I WANT JOB” — bu ingliz tilida yozganingizdan qat’iy nazar, qabul qilinmaydi. To‘g‘risi: “Hello Mr Karimov, I'm writing to apply for the analyst role.” — “Salom Janob Karimov, men analitik lavozimiga ariza topshirish uchun yozmoqdaman.” Slang, katta harf, “u” — bularning hammasi norasmiylashtiradi. Endi professional tarmoq xabarini ko‘ramiz.
scenes.say: A very common mistake: using casual style in professional writing. “HELLO SIR, I WANT JOB” is never accepted. Instead: “Hello Mr Karimov, I'm writing to apply for the analyst role.” No slang, no caps, no abbreviations of “you.”
scenes.say_uz: Juda keng tarqalgan xato: professional yozuvda norasmiy uslub. “HELLO SIR, I WANT JOB” — bu hech qachon qabul qilinmaydi. To‘g‘risi: “Hello Mr Karimov, I'm writing to apply for the analyst role.” — “Salom Janob Karimov, analitik lavozimiga ariza topshirish uchun yozmoqdaman.” Slang, katta harf, “u” — bularning hammasi norasmiylashtiradi.

scenes.title: LinkedIn ulanish xabari
board: Hi Claire — I enjoyed your talk at the fintech meetup last week.
I work in product at Uzum and would love to connect.
scenes.say_native: O‘qing. LinkedIn ulanish xabarini baland ovozda o‘qing. E’tibor bering: ikki qism bor — munosabat (qaerda uchrashgansiz) va nima istayotganingiz (connect). Qisqa, iliq, professional.
scenes.say: Hi Claire — I enjoyed your talk at the fintech meetup last week. I work in product at Uzum and would love to connect. — Behruz
scenes.say_uz: Salom Claire — o‘tgan haftadagi fintech uchrashuvida ma’ruzangizni yoqtirgan edim. Men Uzumda mahsulot bo‘yicha ishlayman va bog‘lanishni xohlayman. — Behruz

scenes.title: LinkedIn xabarining tuzilishi
board: 1. Context — where you met / why you write
3. The ask — connect / a call / a question
scenes.say_native: Professional xabarning tuzilishi: birinchi — kontekst: qayerda uchrashgansiz yoki nega yozyapsiz. Ikkinchi — o‘zingiz haqida bitta gap. Uchinchi — iltimosingiz: bog‘lanish, qo‘ng‘iroq, savol. Uch qismdan ortiq yozmang — odamga vaqtingizni band qilmayapsiz. O‘zbek tilida ham shu uch qism ishlaydi.
scenes.say: The structure of a professional message: first, context — where you met or why you're writing. Second, one line about you. Third, the ask — connect, a call, a question. Never more than three parts — you're not taking their time. The same three parts work in Uzbek.
scenes.say_uz: Professional xabarning tuzilishi: birinchidan — kontekst: qayerda uchrashgansiz yoki nega yozyapsiz. Ikkinchidan — o‘zingiz haqida bitta gap. Uchinchidan — iltimos: bog‘lanish, qo‘ng‘iroq, savol. Uch qismdan ortiq yozmang — odamning vaqtini band qilmayapsiz. O‘zbek tilida ham shu uch qism ishlaydi.

scenes.say: A strong answer: “Hi Sarah — great to meet you at the HR summit. I'm a data analyst looking for new opportunities. I'd love to connect here.” Short, specific, easy to accept. Now the follow-up message after a meeting.

scenes.title: Uchrashuvdan keyingi minnatdorchilik xabari
board: Hi Tom — thanks for your time this morning.
Here's the proposal we discussed, as promised.
scenes.say_native: O‘qing. Uchrashuvdan keyingi xabarni baland ovozda o‘qing. E’tibor bering: uch qism — minnatdorchilik, va’da qilingan material, yordam taklifi.
scenes.say: Hi Tom — thanks for your time this morning. Here's the proposal we discussed, as promised. Happy to answer any questions.

scenes.title: Uchrashuvdan keyingi xabar yozing
board: You had an interview this morning.

scenes.say: You had an interview this morning. Write a thank-you message — three parts: thanks, one specific detail from the interview, and ask to stay in touch. Read it aloud.
scenes.say_uz: Bugun ertalab intervyuda bo‘ldingiz. Minnatdorchilik xabarini yozing — uch qism: rahmat, intervyudagi bitta aniq tafsilot va aloqada qolish iltimosi. Baland ovozda o‘qing.

scenes.title: Tarmoq odobi
board: Never post angry messages in public

examples.t: Thanks for flagging this — I'll look into it today.
examples.uz: E’tiboringiz uchun rahmat — bugun ko‘rib chiqaman.

scenes.say_native: Tarmoq odobi — netiquette: birinchi, 24 soat ichida javob bering, hatto qisqa bo‘lsa ham. Ikkinchi, shikoyatlarni shaxsiy xabarga o‘tkazing. Uchinchi, hech qachon g‘azablangan xabar yozmang — internet hech narsani unutmaydi. To‘rtinchi, hammaga “reply all” yubormang — kerakli odamlarga yetarli. O‘zbek tilida ham xuddi shu qoidalar.
scenes.say: Netiquette: first, reply within 24 hours, even briefly. Second, take complaints offline. Third, never post something angry in public — the internet forgets nothing. Fourth, don't “reply all” when only a few people need it. The same rules apply in Uzbek.
scenes.say_uz: Tarmoq odobi: birinchidan, 24 soat ichida javob bering — hatto qisqa bo‘lsa ham. Ikkinchidan, shikoyatlarni shaxsiy xabarga o‘tkazing. Uchinchidan, g‘azablangan xabarni hamma oldida yozmang — internet hech narsani unutmaydi. To‘rtinchidan, “hammaga javob” yubormang — faqat kerakli odamlarga. O‘zbek tilida ham xuddi shu qoidalar.

scenes.title: To‘g‘ri ohangni tanlang
board: Boss is annoyed about a missed deadline. Choose the best reply:
b) Apologies for the delay — here's the file now.
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Bitta holat: xo‘jayin muddat o‘tgani uchun jahli chiqayapti. Eng yaxshi javobni tanlang: a) “It wasn't my fault!!” b) “Apologies for the delay — here's the file now.” c) 🙄 emoji. Baland ovozda javobingizni ayting va nega deganini tushuntiring.
scenes.say: One situation: your boss is annoyed about a missed deadline. Choose the best reply: “It wasn't my fault!!”, “Apologies for the delay — here's the file now.”, or a rolling-eyes emoji. Say your answer and explain why.
scenes.say_uz: Bitta holat: xo‘jayin muddat o‘tgani uchun jahli chiqayotgan ekan. Eng yaxshi javobni tanlang: “It wasn't my fault!!”, “Apologies for the delay — here's the file now.” yoki 🙄 emoji. Javobingizni baland ovozda ayting va nega ekanini tushuntiring.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: b) “Apologies for the delay — here's the file now.”
Own the mistake, fix it, move on
No excuses, no emoji, no blame
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: to‘g‘risi — b) “Apologies for the delay — here's the file now.” — “Kechikkani uchun uzr — fayl hozir tayyor.” Xatoni o‘z zimmangizga oling, tuzating, oldinga yuring. A) bahonadir, c) esa muloyim emas. Endi yakuniy tekshiruvga o‘tamiz.
scenes.say: Answers: b — “Apologies for the delay — here's the file now.” Own the mistake, fix it, move on. Option a is an excuse; c is not polite. Now the final check.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: b — “Apologies for the delay — here's the file now.” Xatoni zimmangizga oling, tuzating, oldinga yuring. A — bahona; c — muloyim emas. Endi yakuniy tekshiruv.

scenes.title: Yakuniy vazifa: LinkedIn xabari va sharh yozing
board: 1. Write a connection request to a speaker you met.

scenes.say: Final task — write two things. First, a connection request to a speaker you met at a conference. Second, a five-sentence review of a café you visited last week. Read both aloud.

scenes.title: Bugun nimani o‘rgandik
board: Abbreviations: LOL · BRB · ASAP · FYI · BTW
scenes.say_native: Xulosa. Chat qisqartmalarini (LOL, BRB, ASAP, FYI, BTW), emoji madaniyatini, sharh tuzilishini (nima bo‘ldi, nega, nima maslahat berasiz), professional xabarlarning uch qismini (kontekst, siz, iltimos) va tarmoq odobini o‘rgandik. Keyingi darsda so‘zlashuv iboralarini o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say: Recap: abbreviations like LOL, BRB, ASAP, FYI, BTW; emoji culture; review structure — what, why, recommend; the three parts of a professional message — context, you, ask; and netiquette. Next time: conversational phrases.
